req.title: Reject wrong method on /patch
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PATCH on /patch.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /patch must accept PATCH and reject all other HTTP methods with 405. Tests cover: (1) positive - PATCH succeeds with 200 and correct JSON payload keys; (2) negative - GET, POST, PUT, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary - HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-case methods) also return 405; (4) decision-table covering all common wrong methods systematically; (5) BVA on the exact status code 405 vs adjacent codes 404/406.

tests.name: test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: Response body is JSON containing keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload():
    r = client.patch('/patch')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in body, f'Missing key: {key}'

test_patch_method_returns_200_with_expected_payload()

tests.name: test_wrong_methods_all_return_exactly_405_not_404_or_406
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE to /patch
Assert each returns exactly 405, not 404 or 406
trace: R-HTTPBIN-009: Error pathway is HTTP 405 specifically
BVA: 404 and 406 are adjacent codes; 405 is the exact required code
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_wrong_methods_all_return_exactly_405_not_404_or_406():
    wrong_methods = [
        client.get,
        client.post,
        client.put,
        client.delete,
    ]
    for method_fn in wrong_methods:
        r = method_fn('/patch')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f'Expected 405, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 406
        assert r.status_code != 200

test_wrong_methods_all_return_exactly_405_not_404_or_406()

tests.name: test_patch_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key_present
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send PATCH request to /patch with JSON body
expected: Response JSON contains 'json' key with the sent payload
trace: R-HTTPBIN-009: PATCH succeeds; view_patch returns get_dict including 'json'
EP: valid PATCH with body is a representative positive partition
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_patch_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key_present():
    payload = {"key": "value"}
    r = client.patch(
        '/patch',
        data=json.dumps(payload),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert body['json'] == {"key": "value"}

test_patch_with_json_body_returns_200_and_json_key_present()

tests.name: test_patch_status_code_is_not_200_for_wrong_methods_decision_table
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE to /patch
trace: R-HTTPBIN-009: Wrong methods must not succeed (not 200)
DT: all non-PATCH methods map to 405 in the decision table
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_patch_status_code_is_not_200_for_wrong_methods_decision_table():
    cases = [
        ('GET', client.get),
        ('POST', client.post),
        ('PUT', client.put),
        ('DELETE', client.delete),
    ]
    for method_name, method_fn in cases:
        r = method_fn('/patch')
        assert r.status_code != 200, f'{method_name} should not return 200'
        assert r.status_code == 405, f'{method_name} should return 405, got {r.status_code}'

test_patch_status_code_is_not_200_for_wrong_methods_decision_table()
